title: How to organize the charging and device zone | Family Room
description:
Charge the household's phones, tablets, controllers, and headphones in one place, on a surface that can take the heat.

This is the Charging and Device Zone in the Family Room. About 30-45 min.

WHAT DONE LOOKS LIKE
One power strip on a hard surface, four or five labeled cables each ending at a named slot, the empty slots visible during the day, and no charger plugged into any other socket in the room.

THE SIX PASSES
Sort: Lay every cable and plug out in a line and match each one to a device that is in this house and currently work
Straighten: One strip, one slot per device, the owner's name on the slot.
Shine: Wipe each cable end and check the last few centimetres near the plug, where the sheath cracks first.
Safety: Nothing charges on a cushion, a blanket, or a stack of paper.
Standardize: Name labels on the slots, not just on the cables, so an empty slot reads as a missing device rather than as fr
Sustain: When the dishwasher is started for the night, the devices come to the station and stay there until morning.

THE STANDARD YOU LEAVE BEHIND
One strip on a hard surface, one named slot per device, one labeled bag of spare connectors, no charger plugged in anywhere else in the room, and nothing charging on soft material.

Full written steps for this zone, free:
https://6s-success.com/zones/family-room-the-charging-and-device-zone.html

6S Success turns Lean's six-S method into something you can actually do in a house: Sort, Straighten, Shine, Safety, Standardize, Sustain. One small zone at a time, finished in one session, and it stays finished.
